claim: Far-field minimum horizontal effective stress = nu/(1-nu) x vertical effective stress, Terzaghi effective stress (Eq. 11); the Eaton form the engine uses.
quote: sigma_h = nu / (1 - nu) sigma_v, where sigma_i = S_i - P

claim: Eq. 11 holds strictly only for zero lateral strain, uniaxial vertical loading and isotropic linear elasticity.
The calculated Sh is a reopening pressure, the lower bound of leak-off; creation of a new fracture needs more.
quote: field data cluster tightly around predicted initiation or reopening pressures

claim: The reopening and creation modes differ by 3 MPa on average, up to nearly 13 MPa; each mode has sd under 1 MPa.
quote: the SDs of the residuals for each of the "reopening" and "creation" subsets, however, are less than 1 MPa, indicating a strong bimodal distribution localized around these two estimates.

claim: 58 percent of LOTs are at fracture creation, 42 percent at reopening; no correlation with depth, overpressure or VES.
Mixed-mode residuals on 254 LOTs: mean -0.18, sd 0.82, max 2.64 MPa; Hubbert-Willis sd 2.86, max 13.4; Matthews-Kelly sd 2.66, max 19.1.
Matthews and Kelly's empirical Ki performs poorly on the global set and must be calibrated locally.
quote: it must simply be calibrated on a local scale for each application

claim: Eaton 1969's nu trend rests on hydrostatic-pressure and lost-circulation assumptions, not measured stress.
quote: Neither stress nor pore pressure were unambiguously available to Eaton (1969), and thus no clear conclusions about physical models can be drawn from that study.

claim: Overburden from regional density trends integrated from mudline; under 2 percent sensitivity to the trend.
quote: higher or lower by one standard deviation (SD) of the calibration set resulted in pressure differences of less than 2%

claim: For tabular salt within 2-2.5 km, salt tectonics had negligible effect on the stresses; revisit for complex structures.
quote: it is thus assumed that salt tectonics have a negligible impact on stresses for the locations in this study. This assumption should obviously be revisited if more complex salt structures are involved.

claim: A 0.5 MPa shift is 0.17 g/cc (1.4 ppg) EMW at 300 m below mudline but 0.017 g/cc (0.14 ppg) at 3000 m.
quote: A shift of 0.5 MPa for formations at 300 m below mudline, for example, is a change of 0.17 g/cm3 (1.4 lbm/gal) in equivalent mud weight relative to the seafloor

claim: A 25-35 degC cooler mud lowers initiation pressure by 1-4 MPa; such tests fell on minimum stress.
About 10 percent of LOTs exceed the overburden and are still matched, because Sv enters only through the shear modes.
The stress model will not be valid in all basins; all data are passive-margin extensional settings.
quote: it will not be valid in all basins

claim: A Matthews-Kelly fracture gradient near overburden would have misled the example well, where most LOTs fell at Sh.
quote: the actual test results would have come as something of a surprise

claim: Unit conversions used: g/cc x 0.43353 = psi/ft; kPa/m x 0.8510 = ppg EMW.
